title: Monsoon Logistics — hybrid routing & quantization savings hypothesis
body:
Summary:

This is a working savings hypothesis for Monsoon Logistics (routing + customer support embeddings + realtime summarization) after applying a set of Redwood Optimize recommendations. Objective: estimate realistic before/after monthly cost delta, GPU-hour impact, quality risk, and sensitivity to traffic growth and cache hit assumptions. This doc pairs with the linked spreadsheet (cost model + scenario tabs).

High-level recommendation (what we'll test):
- Deploy hybrid routing: route low-cost requests to a 13B quantized variant, keep 70B family for high-quality queries (fallback).
- Enable prefix/KV caching for session-based chat and precompute customer-specific embeddings for 24/7 lookup workloads.
- Apply mixed-precision -> 4-bit quantization where eval shows <1.5% QA accuracy drop for low-critical routes.
- Adjust batching thresholds: increase continuous batching window to 12ms for non-interactive routes and enable adaptive batching for streamed responses.
- Offer reserved Dedicated lanes for high-throughput batch embedding jobs to reduce per-embedding unit cost.

Baseline assumptions (current Monsoon setup):
- Monthly traffic: 1.2B tokens across features (chat 45%, summarization 25%, embeddings 30%).
- Current model mix: hosted 70B family for 80% of live chat/summarize; embeddings served by hosted 70B fine-tuned embedder.
- Current token unit cost (hosted): $0.00009 per token (average across routes).
- Current monthly hosted spend estimate (inc. infra overhead): $108,000.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for chat; p99 < 800ms for summarization (Monsoon wants p95 stricter for chat).

Redwood Optimize applied levers (assumptions used in the spreadsheet):
- Routing split: 65% -> 13B-4bit quantized (fast/cheap), 25% -> 33B-4bit (balanced), 10% -> 70B fp16 (high-quality fallback).
- KV/prefix cache effective hit rate: 28% for session chat, 12% for summarization (due to more unique content). Cache reduces active token generation by rerouting to cached responses or prefix reuse.
- Batching and continuous batching improvements reduce per-request overhead by 14% on token compute time for non-critical routes.
- Dedicated reserved capacity for nightly embedding pipelines reduces per-embedding unit cost by 42% vs hosted burst pricing.
- Quantization factor: 70% relative per-token cost when moving from fp16 to 4-bit execution path on optimized GPUs (plus additional throughput gains).

Estimated before / after (monthly, aggregated) — note: numbers are model outputs from the linked sheet scenario 'optimize_hypothesis_v1':
- Baseline hosted spend: $108,000
- After Apply Redwood Optimize: $66,200
- Absolute savings: $41,800 (~38.7% reduction)
- Monthly GPU-hours baseline (approx): 9,600 GPU-hours
- Post-optimize GPU-hours estimate: 6,100 GPU-hours (36.5% reduction)
- Embedding line item: baseline $28,500 -> optimized dedicated $16,700 (41.5% savings)
- Expected latency impact (p95 chat): baseline 210ms -> optimized route average 180ms for 13B, 240ms for 33B, 320ms for 70B fallbacks. p95 maintained <350ms with current routing split.

Savings breakdown (percent contribution):
- Model family routing + quantization: ~24% of total savings
- Caching (prefix/KV + embedding precompute): ~18%
- Batching & runtime kernel selection: ~9%
- Dedicated embedding lanes + pricing: ~12%
- Miscellaneous (rate-limit tuning, tokenization normalization): ~6%

Quality/regressions and how we measured risk: 
- We ran a 3k-prompt eval set (customer QA + summarization golden set).
- For chat: 13B-4bit shows mean accuracy drop of 0.9% absolute on customer QA pass-rate; 33B-4bit drop 0.3%.
- For summarization: extractive metrics (ROUGE-1) drop <1.2% for 13B on short-form tasks; abstractive long-form shows larger variance.
- Recommendation: only route queries with high-quality flags (length>500 tokens, high-content-importance) to 70B family. Low-importance conversational and template-driven flows can be routed to 13B.

Sensitivity analysis (spreadsheet scenarios included):
- Cache hit rate +/- 10ppt: savings range 28–46% (lower hit -> closer to 28% savings).
- Traffic growth +50% without routing change: optimized run-time savings per month compress to ~30% savings vs baseline (since more fallbacks accumulate).
- Latency SLO tightening (p95 < 200ms): requires raising fraction to 13B or adding more dedicated low-latency capacity; savings drop by ~6–9 percentage points in that scenario.

Implementation plan (minimal viable experimentation):
1) Week 0–2: create gating evals and traffic tagging rules (add 'quality_flag' heuristic to router).
2) Week 2–4: roll out canary routing (start 10% traffic to 13B for low-quality-flag paths). Collect telemetry: token counts, latency distribution, QA pass-rate.
3) Week 4–6: enable prefix caching for sessions in canary cohort. Measure effective hit rate and false-positive refreshes.
4) Week 6–10: move nightly embedding job to Dedicated reserved pool (provisioning + billing change), validate embedding similarity and retrieval latency.
5) Week 10–12: expand routing to target split (65/25/10) if QA/latency metrics acceptable.

Open questions / risks (items to resolve before broad rollout):
- Exact quantization path: which kernels/hardware combos on Monsoon's target regions yield the 70% per-token cost claim? Need perf runs on eu-west and us-west zones.
- Embedding quality drift: does dedicated pipeline rounding/quantization change retrieval precision for long tail queries? Proposed A/B eval for recall@K.
- Billing model change approvals from Monsoon finance: moving to Dedicated for nightly jobs requires contract amendment.
- Edge cases: long-form multi-turn summarization with long context may still require 70B family; we need dynamic length-aware routing.

Action items (owners):
- Marcus Chen: run perf matrix for quantized 13B/33B on eu-west-1 & us-west-2 (due 2025-03-25).
- Priya Nair: extend eval set with 1k long-form summarization examples (due 2025-03-22).
- Leah Martinez (me): schedule Monsoon finance sync and share cost model + sensitivity snapshot (due 2025-03-26).

Appendix (notes on spreadsheet tabs):
- 'assumptions' tab: full list of pricing lines, tokenization rules, payload overheads.
- 'scenario_opt_v1' tab: the numbers above; change percentages live with sliders.
- 'sensitivity' tab: automated tornado chart inputs for cache hit, traffic growth, reserved discount.

This is a draft — please leave comments in the sheet and add slack thread references for any linked PRs. If we get green on perf + eval, next step is a partner-facing one-pager that documents expected unit economics and risk mitigations for Monsoon's procurement team.

Notes to self: double-check embedding dedup rules (we may be overstating precompute benefit if Monsoon has high churn in embedding seeds).
